translationRepairs: He returned to the capital as a vice-director in the Ministry of the Treasury, received the honorary title Grand Master of Palace Leisure, held two vice-director posts in the war ministry's right and left secretariats in turn, and was then promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.

He returned to the capital as a vice-director in the Ministry of the Treasury, received the honorary title Grand Master of Palace Leisure, successively served as vice-director of the Right Office and vice-director of the Ministry of War, then as director of the Left Office and director of the Ministry of War, and was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.

The proposal correctly separates the Right and Left Offices from the Ministry of War, but the four successive posts should be stated individually so that each paired title cannot be mistaken for one combined office.

He entered the capital as vice-director in the Ministry of the Treasury, was given the honorary title Grand Master of Palace Leisure, served successively as two vice-director posts in the right and left secretariats of the Ministry of War, and was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.

He entered the capital as vice-director in the Ministry of the Treasury, was given the honorary title Grand Master of Palace Leisure, served successively as vice-director of the Right Office and vice-director of the Ministry of War, then as director of the Left Office and director of the Ministry of War, and was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.
The proposed office parsing is correct, but naming each of the four posts separately is clearer and more literal than referring to two collective sets of posts.
The emperor also recalled that Jiansu had long served in the Prince of Xiang's household and owed him an old debt of kindness, and approved the choice.
The emperor also recalled that Jiansu had previously served in the household of the Prince of Xiang and had enjoyed his favor, and approved the choice.

The repair correctly reverses the current mistranslation of 有舊恩. This wording makes clear that Jiansu had received the emperor's favor while serving his former princely household, rather than leaving the direction of the favor vague.
In the third month he was relieved of the left vice-directorship and of his duties in government, retiring with the title minister of justice.
In the third month he was appointed left vice-director, relieved of his duties in government, and retired with the title minister of justice.
除左僕射 appoints Wei Jiansu as left vice-director; the distinct phrase 罷知政事 removes him from participation in government. The proposed sequence restores that contrast.
In the third month he was removed from the post of left vice-director, ceased serving in state affairs, and retired with the title Minister of Justice.
In the third month he was appointed to the post of left vice-director, ceased serving in state affairs, and retired with the title Minister of Justice.
The literal field makes the same error by treating 除 as removal. The proposed wording correctly distinguishes appointment to 左僕射 from loss of governing authority.
For escorting the retired emperor to Shu, Jiansu was granted the title Pillar of State with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies and a fief of three hundred households.
For accompanying the retired emperor to Shu, Jiansu was granted the honor of opening an office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies and a fief of three hundred households.

The proposal correctly removes the unrelated title 'Pillar of State,' but 開府 must not disappear from the replacement. The revised wording renders both the privilege of opening an office and its ceremonial parity, while 奉上皇幸蜀 is more naturally 'accompanying' the retired emperor to Shu.

For his merit in escorting the Retired Emperor on the tour to Shu, Jiansu was given the title Pillar of State with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies and an actual fief of three hundred households.

For his merit in attending the Retired Emperor on his journey to Shu, Jiansu was granted the honor of opening an office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies and an actual fief of three hundred households.
The proposed correction removes 'Pillar of State' but omits the 開府 element of the honor. This version preserves that element and avoids implying that Jiansu conducted the imperial party as an escort.
Ti and E both reached the post of Attendant Gentleman; Yi ended as vice-director in the Ministry of Justice, and Guan as secretary in the Secretariat.
Ti and E both reached the post of Attendant Gentleman; Yi ended as vice-director in the Ministry of Justice, and Guan as assistant director of the Palace Library.
The proposal identifies the correct institution, but 丞 is the assistant-director post rather than a generic secretary. 秘書省 is the Palace Library, not the Secretariat.

As a youth he entered office by hereditary privilege as a palace guard attendant. After a favorable evaluation as magistrate of E County he was appointed magistrate of Wannian and rose through the posts of censor, remonstrance official, and secretariat director to Attendant Gentleman, left vice-director of the secretariat, vice-minister of revenue, censor-in-chief, and vice-minister of personnel.

As a youth he entered office by hereditary privilege as a palace guard attendant. After receiving a favorable evaluation as commandant of Hu County, he was appointed commandant of Wannian and rose through the posts of censor, remonstrance official, and gentleman of the Department of State Affairs to Attendant Gentleman, left vice-director of the Department of State Affairs, vice-minister of revenue, censor-in-chief, and vice-minister of personnel.

The proposal fixes 鄠 and distinguishes 尚書省 from the Secretariat, but 縣尉 is a county commandant, not a magistrate. 'Gentleman of the Department of State Affairs' also identifies 尚書郎 more clearly than the proposed hybrid title.

In youth he entered service by hereditary privilege as an armed attendant in the palace guard; from his evaluation as district magistrate of E he was graded for appointment and made magistrate of Wannian; he served successively as censor, remonstrance official, and secretariat director, and was promoted repeatedly to Attendant Gentleman, left vice-director of the Secretariat, vice-minister of revenue, censor-in-chief, and vice-minister of personnel.

In youth he entered service by hereditary privilege as an armed attendant in the palace guard; after his evaluation as commandant of Hu County qualified him for advancement, he was appointed commandant of Wannian; he served successively as censor, remonstrance official, and gentleman of the Department of State Affairs, and was promoted repeatedly to Attendant Gentleman, left vice-director of the Department of State Affairs, vice-minister of revenue, censor-in-chief, and vice-minister of personnel.

The proposal correctly repairs the place name and State Affairs offices, but both occurrences of 尉 denote county commandants. The revision also makes 判入等 an evaluation qualifying him for advancement rather than an opaque grading formula.
When we set out from Mawei yesterday there were also arrangements made.
Earlier, when we set out from Mawei, I also made arrangements.

The proposal correctly recognizes that 昨 cannot mean the previous calendar day here: the court left Mawei before reaching Shu in the seventh month, whereas this speech follows the envoy's arrival in the eighth. 'Earlier' conveys the retrospective sense, and the first-person subject is supplied by the retired emperor's continuing speech.
Yuan abandoned the southern city and fled to Xiangyang, and an edict stripped him of his rank and fief.
Yuan abandoned the city and fled south to Xiangyang, and an edict stripped him of his rank and fief.
棄城 and 南奔 are separate verb phrases: Cui Yuan abandoned the city and fled south. The current 'southern city' attaches 南 to the wrong phrase.
Yuan abandoned the southern city and fled to Xiangyang; an edict stripped him of his rank and fief.
Yuan abandoned the city and fled south to Xiangyang; an edict stripped him of his rank and fief.
The literal field repeats the same attachment error. 南 modifies 奔, specifying southward flight to Xiangyang, rather than 城.
Cui Huan's grandfather Xuanwei had been ennobled as Duke of Boling for his service in the Shenlong coup.
Cui Huan's grandfather Xuanwei had been ennobled as Prince of Boling Commandery for his service in the Shenlong coup.
博陵郡王 is a commandery princely title, not a dukedom. The proposed title preserves the explicit 郡王 rank.
Cui Huan's grandfather Xuanwei was a meritorious servant of the Shenlong coup and was enfeoffed as Duke of Boling.
Cui Huan's grandfather Xuanwei was a meritorious servant of the Shenlong coup and was enfeoffed as Prince of Boling Commandery.
The literal field likewise mistranslates 郡王 as duke. 'Prince of Boling Commandery' restores the stated rank.
His father Zhang was a noted scholar who rose to vice-minister of rites.
His father Qu was a noted scholar who rose to vice-minister of rites.
璩 is Cui Huan's father's given name, Qu; 'Zhang' has no basis in the Chinese. The replacement agrees with the surname inherited from the surrounding Cui genealogy.
His father Zhang was renowned for literary learning and reached the post of vice-minister of rites.
His father Qu was renowned for literary learning and reached the post of vice-minister of rites.
The literal field contains the same unsupported name. 璩 is read Qu and identifies Cui Huan's father.
In the first year of Zhenyuan (785) he personally performed the Southern Suburbs sacrifice and served as commissioner for the grand rites.
In the first year of Zhenyuan (785), when the emperor personally performed the Southern Suburbs sacrifice, Zong served as commissioner for the grand rites.
The implicit subject of 親祠 is Emperor Dezong, while Cui Zong is the subject of 為大禮使. The proposal correctly separates the sovereign performing the sacrifice from the official administering its rites.
In the first year of Zhenyuan, he personally sacrificed at the Southern Suburbs and served as commissioner for the grand rites.
In the first year of Zhenyuan, the emperor personally sacrificed at the Southern Suburbs; Zong served as commissioner for the grand rites.
The literal field wrongly assigns both actions to Cui Zong. In this regnal context the emperor personally performs the suburban sacrifice and Zong serves as grand-rites commissioner.
Du Hongjian was a clansman of the former chancellor Xian.
Du Hongjian was a clansman of the former chancellor Du Xian.
暹 refers to Du Xian, the former chancellor and senior clansman named by the shared surname 杜. Supplying the surname prevents an unnecessary ambiguity without changing the kinship claim.
More than a year later he was recalled as right vice-director of the secretariat, vice-minister of personnel, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and appointed commissioner of ritual.

More than a year later he was recalled as right vice-director of the Department of State Affairs, vice-minister of personnel, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and appointed commissioner of ritual.
尚書右丞 belongs to the Department of State Affairs, not the Secretariat. The proposed correction changes only the misidentified institution.

After more than a year he was summoned and appointed right vice-director of the Secretariat, vice-minister of personnel, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and made commissioner of ritual.

After more than a year he was summoned and appointed right vice-director of the Department of State Affairs, vice-minister of personnel, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and made commissioner of ritual.
The literal field makes the same institutional error. 尚書省 is the Department of State Affairs; the neighboring reference to 二聖 in s0190 does not alter Du Hongjian's subject or office sequence.
In the eighth month of the third year, Prince Jin of Dai became guardian of the eastern capital, deputy commander of Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East, while retaining his grand councilorship.
In the eighth month of the third year, he replaced Wang Jin as guardian of the eastern capital, deputy commander of Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East, while retaining his grand councilorship.
代 is the verb 'replaced' and 王縉 is the official Wang Jin. The current reading invents a Prince Jin of Dai and wrongly makes him the sentence's subject instead of Du Hongjian.

In the eighth month of the third year, Prince Jin of Dai became guardian of the eastern capital, served as deputy commander of Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East circuits, and remained grand councilor as before.

In the eighth month of the third year, he replaced Wang Jin as guardian of the eastern capital, served as deputy commander of Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East circuits, and remained grand councilor as before.
The literal field repeats the segmentation error. Du Hongjian replaced Wang Jin as eastern-capital guardian and retained his own grand councilorship.
